Autoresearch

You already run Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenAI Codex, pi, or Muse. Point one of them at a problem and it will keep improving it while you sleep.

The idea is Karpathy's: one constraint, one mechanical metric, then let the agent iterate on its own. Gains compound.

You set the GOAL. The agent runs the LOOP. You wake up to results.

You don't need AGI. You need a goal, a metric, and a loop that never quits.

The core skill, bundled runtime, installation, and verification surface work with Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenAI Codex, pi, and Muse. Hook guardrails ship for Claude Code (native hooks) and pi (extension events).

When the metric stalls, the loop forks. Cai et al. (arXiv:2610.07447) showed this works. At 33% and 66% of the budget, or after 5 iterations with no keep, the loop forks fresh-context branches from the best commit so far, runs each briefly, and keeps the winner. Half the branches pick their own ideas (randomness). The other half each get a distinct experiment from a stateless Advisor that reads the results log (Zhang et al., arXiv:2610.07625). Guided: R sets the split. The orchestrator answers a plateau with FORK before it gives up. See guide/autoresearch.md.

Bumblebee collects inventory. Read-only, on macOS and Linux developer endpoints: packages, extensions, developer-tool metadata.

It answers one question. An advisory names a package, extension, or version. Which of your developer machines have it on disk right now?

Mean verifier reward: +21.12 pp

SkillsBench tests whether AI agents can use Skills to complete professional tasks across different domains. It measures how much better a model gets at solving complex real-world work when it has specialized Skills on hand.

Most benchmarks hand each task the one Skill it needs. That's not how production works. So we rebuilt SkillsBench for a large-scale multi-Skill setting: every task runs in a global environment with all 195 specialized Skills installed, and nothing else changes. The question is simple. Can an agent dig through a big pool of installed Skills, pick the right ones, and wire them into a workflow that actually finishes the job?

We ran vibeskills v4.1.0 on SkillsBench using DeepSeekV4Flash-VE and OpenHands as the baseline evaluation setup. Against the baseline without vibeskills, the mean verifier reward went up 21.12 percentage points. Token consumption dropped 29.6%. Tool calls dropped 33.1%.

Semantic version control built on Git.

Rather than reporting lines changed, sem reports which entities changed: functions, methods, classes.

Releases

sem sits on top of Git as a semantic version control tool. Using tree-sitter, it parses your code and pulls out every function, class, and method as an entity, then diffs entities rather than lines. The result is a message like "function blahh was modified" instead of "lines x-y changed."

No setup is needed; it works in any Git repo.

Cloud-backed queries are opt-in per repo, and logging in uploads nothing or sends no query. The cloud consent flow covers the public/private repo states, the preview screen, a local audit log, and forget controls.
